stops.note: from tegere 'to cover'; roof tiles made by the army were often stamped with the legion's number
Anglo-Saxons knew tiles mostly from Roman ruins; St Albans Abbey's tower, built from the 1070s, reuses thousands of Roman bricks and tiles from Verulamium
the i-sound came from a shortened form tigle, as in German Ziegel 'brick'

current_meaning: a thin slab used to cover roofs, floors or walls
